messages:
incident-bot: Heads-up: postmortem 'db-connection-throttle' action #2 (owner: @sam) is 6 days overdue. Please update status or reassign. Tracker: https://redwood.company/pm/db-connection-throttle/actions :rotating_light:
sam: Sorry — been pulled into ops support for the outage follow-ups. I still have the connection-pool patch and the test harness to land. Will try to finish by EOD.
noor: @sam can you paste the failing stress test output? We need to know if this will impact the lock-step rollout scheduled for tomorrow.
sam: Snippet:
```
2026-03-20T22:05:12Z WARN pool.go:178 max_open 500 -> reached
2026-03-20T22:05:13Z ERROR conn.go:43 connection_close: too many idle
```
noor: That looks like pool sizing + leak. If patch not in, we should postpone the rollout.
ops-oncall: We also observed similar throttles in region-e last week; this smells like a recurring pattern. @sam do you need a hand? If you can't hit ETA, we'll reassign to infra-leads.
sam: I can do pairing tomorrow morning 08:00 PT with @noor. Concern: running the harness against prod-like clusters needs ops window.
rachel_pm: If this slips beyond Thursday, we must notify impacted customers and freeze the release. Please update the tracker with a contingency plan.
incident-bot: Reminder set: follow up with @sam in 24h.
(Next day)
noor: Quick status: ran targeted unit + integration tests, patch reduces connection churn in harness by ~70%. Still need to validate multi-region failover.
sam: Pushing a WIP PR: https://git.redwood/serving/pulls/881 — includes pooled client metrics and a GC tweak.
ops-oncall: FYI infra maintenance window open tonight 00:30-01:30 UTC. We can run multi-region harness then. Whoever's running, please invite @ops-oncall for rollback readiness.
sam: Booking; will run canary after midnight.
(After maintenance window)
sam: Canary run executed, region-c passed, region-e still showed intermittent throttles but much reduced. Collected traces attached to tracker.
noor: Traces indicate a fallback path in the client that creates extra conn objects under high qps. I'll add a guard and a test.
ops-oncall: Because this is recurring, I'm going to nominate infra-leads as secondary owners in the tracker so we can escalate if needed. @sam OK with that?
sam: Fine, please set secondary. I retain primary and will finish final tests.
incident-bot: Action #2 updated: owner @sam, secondary @infra-leads, status 'verifying'. Reminder set for 48h.
rachel_pm: Please also add a monitoring rule: alert if region_conn_open > 450 for 10m. This prevents silent regressions.
oor: Added prometheus alert: db_region_conn_open_total > 450 for 10m. Dashboards updated.
(48h later)
sam: Final PR merged and deployed. Canary to 20% then 100% with no throttles. p95 stable.
ops-oncall: Verified in both regions, no regressions.
incident-bot: Action #2 moved to 'done' by @sam in tracker.
rachel_pm: Closing the action. Noting recurring-incident tag and scheduling a reliability review agenda item.
sam: Left final notes in postmortem: root cause = client fallback creating transient connections under high QPS, fix = connection guard + improved metrics. Thanks for the assist. :white_check_mark:
infra-leads: We'll follow up in the reliability review with long-term mitigations (connection pooling redesign).
